name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean after redistricting
Jerry Carl's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 4%
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean and the favorable post-redistricting fundamentals point strongly Republican, and Jerry Carl's roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge plus half a million dollars in outside support reinforce that. Markets price a Democratic win at about 4%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Clyde Jones Jr. competitive, or a major scandal or independent-spending surge on the Democratic side, would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its R+17 partisan lean makes it strongly Republican terrain. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Jerry Carl holds a decisive financial advantage, raising about $1.16 million with $367,000 on hand and $547,000 in outside support, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $86,000. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 4% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any evidence of competition.
